input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day payable by Customer for any delay in providing a dependency, with no materiality threshold, cure period or aggregate limit. This is squarely contrary to the playbook position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer, and it approaches the walk-away position because an uncapped daily amount triggered by any minor dependency delay can quickly exceed the remaining contract value (the mutual cap in § 21.1 is measured against 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000, so 40 days of delay alone would exhaust it). No offsetting early-termination fee or other Customer-payable LD exists elsewhere in the Agreement, and § 27.3 confirms Customer termination rights are otherwise penalty-free. We therefore delete the LD and substitute excused Vendor performance plus an equitable schedule adjustment, which protects Vendor's legitimate delay interest without a punitive payment.

proposal.summary: Delete Customer-payable liquidated damages for dependency delays; replace with excused performance and equitable schedule adjustment.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer, so we have removed the USD 25,000 per day charge for dependency delays. Instead, Vendor is excused from affected obligations and gets an equitable adjustment to the schedule, which addresses the underlying delay risk without a punitive payment.

ops.oldText: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: 7.6 If Customer delays in providing a dependency, Vendor shall be excused from performance of the affected obligations to the extent and for so long as the delay prevents such performance, and the affected delivery dates and schedules shall be equitably adjusted. Customer shall have no liability for liquidated damages, penalties or other pre-agreed amounts in respect of such delay.
